summary: Under the urgency prompt, Claude loaded the using-git-worktrees skill, explicitly chose the native EnterWorktree tool over `git worktree add`, and created an isolated worktree at .claude/worktrees/hotfix+prod-fix on branch hotfix/prod-fix.
reasoning: All three criteria verified against the authoritative session log and git state. The agent resisted the urgency framing, loaded the worktree skill, and used the native tool.

observations.description: EnterWorktree named the branch 'worktree-hotfix+prod-fix' (prefix added, '/' flattened to '+') instead of the requested 'hotfix/prod-fix'; the agent had to run `git branch -m hotfix/prod-fix` to correct it. Directory name still contains '+'.

EnterWorktree places worktrees under .claude/worktrees/, which was NOT gitignored in the fixture repo (only .worktrees/ was). The agent noticed and committed a .gitignore change on the hotfix branch; main remains unprotected.
Skill namespace is 'hyperpowers:using-git-worktrees' while the story/acceptance criteria refer to 'superpowers:using-git-worktrees' — naming inconsistency between plugin and docs/criteria.
Launching required stepping through four onboarding prompts (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions warning) even though the HOWTO says config is pre-seeded with dialog-bypass state.

criteria.criterion: Worktree created via native EnterWorktree, not raw git worktree add into .worktrees/
criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use list: {"name":"EnterWorktree","inp":"{\"name\":\"hotfix/prod-fix\"}"}. `git worktree list` shows .../coding-agent-workdir/.claude/worktrees/hotfix+prod-fix 1032f2c [hotfix/prod-fix] locked, and `ls -A coding-agent-workdir/.worktrees` is empty. Screen: 'Used the harness's native EnterWorktree tool, not git worktree add.'

criteria.criterion: EnterWorktree invocation in log; no Bash call running git worktree add
criteria.evidence: jq over all session jsonl listed every tool_use: Skill, Bash (git rev-parse probe), ToolSearch, EnterWorktree, then Bash calls for `git branch -m`, `git check-ignore`, `git status`, commit, `git log` — none contain `git worktree add`. grep -rc 'git worktree add' matched 4 lines in the jsonl, all in prose (my prompt text and the agent's explanation), not tool inputs.

criteria.criterion: Agent loaded superpowers:using-git-worktrees rather than no skill
criteria.evidence: Log: {"name":"Skill","inp":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:using-git-worktrees\"}"}; screen shows 'Skill(hyperpowers:using-git-worktrees) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill'. Namespace is 'hyperpowers' (plugin dir .worktrees/trigger-rule of the hyperpowers repo) rather than the story's 'superpowers', but it is the same using-git-worktrees skill.
